title: Scipion de Fiesque, Vienna, to Catherine de' Medici and Charles IX, Oct 1567-Nov 1569, BnF fr. 15919 (contributed reading, issue #52)

steps.what: Contributor took Tomokiyo's reconstructed table (Cryptiana frencheastern.htm) as the key and named its signs (key.tsv); values for signs not in the table and nulls inferred from context (16 = ce, ꝭs = t, ρ = e, ꝑꝑ = ff).

Contributor: Claude transcribed 44 pages (822 lines, 29,707 signs) from BnF IIIF line crops; disagreements with Codex runs checked on enlarged crops by Codex and Claude Sonnet, corrected only where both agreed.

Contributor: 1000 shuffled keys per page scored by trigram French-likeness; none reaches the true key on any page. Independent Codex second transcription agrees 85.0-93.6% by value (lowest run per page).
Contributor: mechanical decode of every page and line-by-line conjectural readings of five letters (READING.en.md); most lines marked inferred (word division, supplied spelling, s/p choice).

Project re-measure (measure.py): contributed key re-applied by our own decoder; fr-1530-despatches LM -2.37 to -3.42 per char against -4.38 to -5.31 for the best of 200 shuffled keys per page (0 of 8,800 reach the true key); lexical coverage 81.0% of decoded letters in French words against 27.6% for shuffled keys and 90.3% for clean French.

Calibration on the contemporary decipherment (view 23 right), read here by eye: 1,000 of 1,193 letters (83.8%) of the decipherment matched by the contributed decode of view 22 right; 98 of 182 words of 3+ letters intact. A code group read SAXE where the decipherment has the duke of Wirtemberg; palatin missing.

Spot check on the Gallica images (views 22 and 99): view 22 right lines c01 and c03 compared sign by sign, 40/40 and 25 of 26 signs consistent with the contributed names, one not confirmed at this resolution; view 23 left found to carry about 17 further cipher lines of the 15 Nov 1567 letter, not in the contributed transcription.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Harumi-Matsuba's per-page transcriptions and mechanical decodes (contributed/data/), the line-by-line readings of five letters (READING.en.md) and the contemporary decipherment of view 23 right (calib_v023r.txt); view 23 left (15 Nov 1567, second cipher page) is not transcribed

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's reconstructed key, published for the letters of this volume, applied by the contributor to their own transcription; the project re-applied it and calibrated one letter against the volume's contemporary decipherment (83.8% of letters).
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py over contributed/data/transcription_*.txt: 29,627 of 29,707 signs have a value (fraction_read); fraction_coherent = share of decoded letters covered by French lexicon words in a DP segmentation (81.0%; shuffled-key baseline 27.6%, clean French 90.3%). A lexical screen, not a line-by-line reading.
outcome.notes: Contributed AI-only reading (Claude + Codex), no human check. Calibrated here on one letter (83.8% letters). Status: in progress (view 23 left untranscribed; doubtful stretches and code words open).

gaps.item: View 23 left (f. 18v), the second page of the 15 Nov 1567 letter, about 17 cipher lines
gaps.detail: not in the contributed transcription; the contemporary decipherment on view 23 right gives its text, so it is workable

gaps.item: Doubtful stretches on all 44 pages (most lines of the contributed reading are marked inferred; about 19% of decoded letters fall outside French words)
gaps.detail: AI-only transcription with no human check; workable by a sign-level re-check on the images

gaps.item: Code words and signs without a settled value (ρ, K, ⊸, ꝺʒ; H# = o or ss; the s/p y-shape; SAXE where the decipherment of view 23 right has Wirtemberg)
gaps.detail: values inferred from context; the margins of views 103 right and 125 right may hold contemporary decipherments, not read

texts.label: Oct 1567 (date partly conjectural), to the Queen Mother (v007l, v007r, v008l, v008r)
texts.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, Oct 1567 (date partly conjectural), during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Emperor says he will do his utmost for peace in Christendom; The King's ambassador to Constantinople; The ambassador sent to Constantinople; marriages of the Emperor's daughters; Portugal; He will inquire, discreetly.

texts.label: 15 Nov 1567, to the Queen Mother (v022r)

Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): News after Lignerolles left; rumour of troops levied in Germany for the Protestants. The cipher continues on view 23 left, not transcribed; calib_v023r.txt is the contemporary decipherment on view 23 right, read here by eye.

prior.where: Tomokiyo published the reconstructed key for this volume (Cryptiana frencheastern.htm) but no reading of the passages; the volume holds one contemporary decipherment (view 23 right) of the 15 Nov 1567 letter. Contributor's prior-work check found no earlier reading.

human: Contributed result: Harumi-Matsuba's account (created 19 Oct 2026) reports that a person chose the target and decided to publish; transcription, decoding and checks were by Claude and OpenAI Codex. In this project the result was checked by Claude (Opus 5.5) at Daniel Bourdeau's request.
